description: Repeat-scope parity cases generated by @json-render/core (PDF catalog: repeat, $item, $index, $bindItem). Scope: "scope" is { "item"?, "index"?, "basePath"? } = core PropResolutionContext { repeatItem, repeatIndex, repeatBasePath } with stateModel = "state"; a missing key means undefined (outside a repeat). fn "resolvePropValue": { value, scope, state } -> expected = resolvePropValue(value, ctx). fn "resolveBindings": { props, scope, state } -> expected = resolveBindings(props, ctx) (prop -> state path), null when there are none. fn "resolveActionParam": { value, scope, state } -> expected = resolveActionParam(value, ctx); note a top-level $item resolves to the item's absolute state PATH here, not its value. fn "evaluateVisibility": { condition, scope, state } -> expected boolean. fn "resolveRepeatStatePath": { statePath, basePath? } -> expected path string (null + "undefined": true when core returns undefined). fn "resolveRepeatItemStatePath": { statePath, index } -> expected path string. fn "renderTree": { spec } -> expected tree mirroring @json-render/react-pdf renderToBuffer's element walk: node = { key, type, props (resolved), scope? { index, basePath } (present inside a repeat), children }. Order per element: visible (in the current scope) -> resolve props (current scope) -> skip unknown types (only PDF catalog components render: upstream's 14 plus the 6 form components) -> if repeat: statePath via resolveRepeatStatePath(statePath, current basePath) (undefined -> element not rendered), items = getByPath(state, path) ?? [], and for each item i the element's children render with { item, index: i, basePath: resolveRepeatItemStatePath(path, i) }; otherwise children render in the current scope. Missing child keys are skipped. JSON has no undefined: inside objects a key that resolves to undefined is omitted, inside arrays it becomes null. "undefinedPaths" (on value-returning cases) lists JSON Pointers into the result whose core value is undefined, "" for the result itself.

cases.name: $item field on a primitive item is undefined
$bindItem reads state, not the item (basePath wins)
$template bare name falls back to state when the item lacks it
$template bare name falls back to state when the item value is null
$template bare name outside a repeat reads /name
nested object and array members resolve in scope
$item in an action param resolves to the item's state path
$item "" in an action param is the item path
$state in an action param reads state
$item action param outside a repeat is undefined
nested $item in an action param object resolves to the value (only top level is a path)
$item with leading slash joins the base
$item statePath outside a repeat is undefined
item path with an empty base
form fields inside a repeated FieldSet resolve per item
repeat renders children once per item with $item / $index / visible
nested repeat with an item-relative statePath and $bindItem
repeat container props resolve in the outer scope; missing / null arrays render no items
hidden repeat container, $item statePath outside a repeat, missing children and unknown types are skipped
